speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms better, could you tell me your age and whether you have noticed any swollen lymph nodes or an enlarged abdomen? Also, has your fever been persistent or intermittent over these three weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing generalized fatigue and easy bruising for 3 weeks. Over the past week, she has developed a fever and severe leg pain that wakes her up at night.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does she have any bone tenderness, particularly in the long bones, and have you noticed any bleeding from the gums or nose? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential and Peripheral Blood Smear.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 10.1 g/dL, Leukocyte Count: 63,000/mm3 (elevated), Platelet Count: 27,000/mm3 (decreased)

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the severe bone pain, bruising, and markedly elevated white cell count with low platelets, I suspect acute leukemia. REQUEST TEST: Bone Marrow Aspirate and Biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Predominantly immature cells that are positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT.

speaker: Doctor
text: The bone marrow results confirm Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL). DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
